title: Ingest correlation-id autopsy notes
content:
Summary:
I was handed an escalation: downstream services report missing or inconsistent X-Correlation-Id values in logs and traces for ~3% of user requests over the last 48h. This doc is a running autopsy: commands tried, concrete failures, quick experiments, hypotheses to validate, and next steps. Notes are messy — mainly personal scratchpad to keep the sequence reproducible.

Key symptoms observed:
- Spike in 'orphaned traces' in honeycomb (trace without parent span) between 2026-01-28 03:00–06:30 UTC.
- Kibana: high volume of logs where request_id is present but x-correlation-id header is blank.
- Ingest service (ingest-gateway) latency and error rates are nominal; no obvious 5xx surge.
- Sampler counts: sampling ratio unchanged; but a fraction of traces arrive with server span missing correlation header.

Short timeline:
- 2026-01-27 22:40 UTC: first pager alert (customer reported missing trace linking).
- 2026-01-27 23:05 UTC: triage, opened JIRA-OBS-1147.
- 2026-01-28 00:30–02:15 UTC: ran live checks and injected test events (see experiments).
- 2026-01-28 03:15 UTC: observed pattern aligned with LB config reloades.

Immediate reproduction attempts (commands used):
- curl to ingestion endpoint with explicit header (expected to be echoed into logs):
  curl -v -X POST https://ingest.redwood.test/v1/events -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Correlation-Id: test-abc-123' -d '{"msg":"correlation test"}'
  -> 200 OK, response body has trace_id but NOT guaranteed header echo in logs.

- Quick local tail of ingester pod logs: (kubectl from jumpbox)
  kubectl -n prod logs deploy/ingest-gateway --since=10m | rg "test-abc-123" -n
  -> 0 matches (bad).

- Confirm header reachability to backend service (bypassing LB)
  forward port then curl to internal svc:
  kubectl -n prod port-forward svc/ingest-gateway 8080:80 &
  curl -H 'X-Correlation-Id: test-abc-123' http://localhost:8080/health
  -> service sees header (CHECK: header present in app-level logs).
  Suggests LB might be stripping or rewriting header occasionally.

- Inspect envoy LB (edge-proxy) config dump during window:
  kubectl -n infra exec deploy/envoy-edge -- curl localhost:9901/config_dump > /tmp/edge-cfg.json
  rg "x-correlation" /tmp/edge-cfg.json -n || true
  -> header_list set to allow x-correlation-id in 85% of configs, some active listeners missing header_list config (likely config rollout timing mismatch).

Concrete error snippets I captured:
- Downstream app log lines (redacted):
  [2026-01-28T03:22:10Z] INFO request_id=7f8a4b2a - received /api/track - x_correlation_id="" - user=foo

- Honeycomb trace fragment (missing parent header):
  { span_id: "d492...", trace_id: "eb9a...", name: "ingest.receive", tags: { sample_rate: "0.01" }, parent_id: null }

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Edge LB config rollout occasionally omits header whitelist, so requests passing through a subset of listeners lose x-correlation-id. (high priority)
2) Sidecar (prometheus/log forwarder) header normalization rule strips header if malformed — some clients send funky values causing drop. (medium)
3) HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.1 gateway translation bug scrubs unknown headers under backpressure. (low-medium)
4) Sampling/collector bug: collector aggregates logs and emits traces without parent when it cannot stitch due to async write ordering. (low)

What I tested and outcomes:
- Edge listener config check (see above) -> found slight divergence in active configs; captured when scaling event at 03:08 UTC.
- Simulated malformed header (control chars)
  curl -H $'X-Correlation-Id: test-\x00bad' ...
  -> ingress rejected (400) in 100% of tries. So malformed headers get rejected, not silently stripped. Reduces plausibility of hypothesis #2 for the majority of cases.
- Burst injection to exercise translation layer: 10k reqs at t=03:05 UTC using k6, measuring header retention ratio.
  -> retention ~97.1% consistent with observed ~3% loss.
  -> correlated with times when edge-proxy pod was rolling (k8s started new pod, some requests hit the new pod without header whitelist).

Debug breadcrumbs / artifacts collected:
- /tmp/edge-cfg.json (config dumps from all envoy-edge instances at 03:12–03:20).
- kibana query IDs: saved-query: OBS-1147-orphans-20260128
- example request ids w/ missing header: 7f8a4b2a, f3c1d9b2, a19b220c (copied from downstream logs).
- honeycomb traces list: trace links attached to JIRA-OBS-1147.

Quick mitigation performed (and result):
- At 2026-01-28 06:00 UTC rolled back recent envoy-edge listener change (the change had been rolled out 03:05 UTC).
  Result: orphan rate dropped from ~3% to ~0.1% over 40m.
- Added a temporary rule at edge to always preserve X-Correlation-Id and reject config changes that do not include header whitelist. (manual guard, pending automation).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did the rollout push out a config variant that lacked header_list? CI check should catch this. Add a unit test to ensure allowed headers invariant.
- Are there any other headers used for trace stitching? (x-request-id, x-b3-spanid, etc.) Confirmed other headers preserved.
- Need a replay script to re-ingest those orphaned requests for customer debug (ethical/privacy check first).
- Run a coordinated chaos run: simulate rolling update and measure header retention under different connection draining windows.

Small scripts / reproducible experiment notes:
- Python quickly send a batch with unique correlation ids and record which ones appear in backend logs: (pseudo)
  import requests, uuid
  ids = [str(uuid.uuid4()) for _ in range(2000)]
  for id in ids:
    requests.post('https://ingest.redwood.test/v1/events', headers={'X-Correlation-Id': id}, json={'m':1})
  # collect via kibana query filtering on message content and match ids

- k6 script used for burst test: repo: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-loadtests/k6/retain-header.js (linked above).

Notes to self (things I want to check later):
- Pull config history from gitops timeline around 2026-01-28 02:45–03:20 UTC: which PR applied? Who approved? PR number in gitops: ops/gp-487 (confirm).
- Ask infra team if the ingress controller has a hotfix path that ensures header_list is always present on new listeners.
- Add an alert for config drift: any listener without header_list should be flagged.

Suggested postmortem items (short):
- Root cause: incomplete config rollout for envoy-edge (missing header whitelist on subset of listeners during scaling event).
- Immediate fix: rollback + guard rule to preserve X-Correlation-Id.
- Remediation: CI validation + e2e test for header preservation across rolling updates; add canary check that verifies header retention before traffic shift.
- Long-term: improve observability on config distribution (per-listener health + invariant checks).

If anyone reading this wants to reproduce or pick up: start with /tmp/edge-cfg.json and the k6 script. Ping me (Priya) in #obs-debug if you want the raw dumps or to run experiments together.

End of notebook (for now) — will convert to a cleaner playbook if we confirm root cause and mitigation path.
